title: Understanding Low Water Pressure: Mineral Scale Restricting Pipe Flow
description: An educational breakdown of how internal mineral scale accumulation reduces pipe diameter and restricts dynamic water flow to fixtures.
image_prompt: A professional educational cross-section cutaway shot of an aging metal water supply pipe, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio. The interior cutaway clearly shows heavy white mineral scale and corrosion tuberculation built up along the pipe walls, significantly narrowing the internal diameter. The background is a clean neutral mechanical workshop setting with studio lighting highlighting the contrast between the clean pipe exterior and the restricted interior pathway. Pipe fittings are visible on the ends. Clean spatial composition with empty space at the top and bottom third for text overlays. Photorealistic depth of field, sharp focus on the mineral blockage, no text, no graphics, no logos, no watermarks, physically accurate plumbing geometry.
visual_story: The visual focuses on a physical cross-section of a water line choked by hard water minerals. Viewers immediately observe how scale buildup restricts the internal pathway of the pipe. This illustrates why static pressure may seem normal when fixtures are off, but dynamic pressure drops significantly once water begins moving through narrowed lines or aerators.

on_image_text.explanation: Mineral scale reduces internal pipe diameter, restricting active water flow.
on_image_text.takeaway: Check aerators first before assuming municipal supply issues.
